results.title: H100 SXM median closed at $3.70, week of 21 September 2026
highlights:
H100 SXM median closed at $3.70, week of 21 September 2026

Analysis · September 28, 2026 · figures frozen on that day

# H100 SXM median closed at $3.70, week of 21 September 2026

The figure$3.70 Weekly median, H100 SXM on-demand, week of 2026-09-21 (final) · $3.70 per GPU-hour from 26 quotes across 24 providers, against $3.90 the week before (-5.1%) · read Sep 27, 23:40 UTC · source · live page

Every figure below is a reading this site published - a rate read on a provider's own page, or a value of the index computed from such rates - listed with its source under the text and frozen as of that day: prices move, and a dated piece says what was true on its date. The live tables are linked beside each figure.

The week of 21 September 2026 closed with our H100 SXM median at $3.70 per GPU-hour, taken from 26 publicly listed on-demand rates across 24 clouds. The week of 14 September closed at $3.90 across 21 quotes and 19 clouds; the week of 7 September at $3.92 across 20 and 18. Week on week that is a fall of 5.1%. Of the quotes read in both of the last two weeks, one listed rate changed.

## Nineteen of twenty rates read the same

Twenty (provider, region) pairs were quoted in both weeks. Nineteen of them were read at the same figure in both. The one that changed is Verda, the cloud our table still files under the id DataCrunch: $3.3475 per GPU-hour in the week of 14 September and $3.555 in the week of 21 September, a rise of 6.2%. Its price page printed 3.555 when this piece was written on 2026-09-28; our tables round it to $3.56, and the week before they rounded it to $3.35.

That gap between a falling median and a nearly unchanged set of rates is what the second column of the Price Index exists to measure. The base-100 index is chain-linked: each week’s link is the geometric mean of the week-over-week ratios of the pairs quoted in both weeks, so a cloud joining or leaving contributes no ratio at all. Nineteen ratios of exactly 1 and one of 1.062 give a link of 1.003, and the index moved from 100.1 to 100.4 against the week of 7 September as 100 — a rise of 0.3% in the same week the dollar median fell 5.1%.

...

Six pairs entered the basket for the first time: Atlas Cloud at $2.95, Civo and HexGrid’s Secure Cloud at $2.99, Hyperbolic at $3.19, Canopy Wave at $3.25 and Neysa at $4.39.

...

One pair left. GMI Cloud’s $2.00 was the cheapest quote in the week of 14 September; the figure itself did not change, but from the read of 19 September, an hour after our 16:38 UTC read, we file it under H100 80GB (form factor not stated) rather than H100 SXM, so it is no longer in this card’s basket.

...

Every figure above is listed under this piece with the page it was read from and the time of the read. The week has a receipt of its own, `2026-W39.csv`: one row per quote read for that week, with its source link, its read time and whether it entered the median. It carries 31 rows — the 26 that entered, and 5 read and kept out under a named rule: Gcore, Scaleway and Seeweb because they list in euros, and two Vast.ai rows because a marketplace floor is not a rate card. With 26 quotes the median is the midpoint of the thirteenth and fourteenth of them in order, which are Verda’s and Nebius’s $3.85. The week is marked final, which means it is not recomputed when later reads arrive. Nothing here is forecast and nothing here is advice: the piece states what 26 price pages were read at over one week, and which of them moved.

results.title: H100 price per hour, October 2026: 11 clouds compared · ClearCompute
results.author: Ronit Ahuja
highlights:
The short answer

On 5 October 2026, one H100 80GB SXM listed at $2.69 to $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand across nine clouds, and the Vast.ai marketplace median was $1.80. Five specialist clouds charged between $3.20 and $4.50. The hyperscalers charged $6.88 (AWS), $11.06 (Google Cloud) and $12.29 (Azure), though a three-year commitment brings them down to between $2.97 and $5.40. For an inference server, four things matter as much as the rate: the smallest unit you can rent, egress, billing increments and how fast the price is moving.

## H100 prices on 5 October 2026#

We read each provider's public price list or pricing API on the same day. Where a provider only sells eight-GPU machines, we divided the machine's price by eight.

## Prices rose this autumn#

- Nebius raised on-demand prices on 1 October: H100 by 17% ($3.85 to $4.50), H200 by 20% and B200 by 19%.
- AWS announced a 15% rise in EC2 Capacity Block prices from 7 October, taking a P5 H100 from $5.19 to $5.97 per GPU-hour.

Any price survey goes stale within weeks, this one included. For today's number, live trackers such as gpufinder.dev, which polls 22 vendors every hour, and SkyPilot's GPU Compass are better sources. A survey is more useful for explaining what the number buys.

results.title: Verda GPU Cloud 怎么选？原 DataCrunch 的 A100、H100、H200、B200 价格和 10 分钟计费 | 智机玄同
results.author: 智机玄同 发布于 2026年10月9日 3 分钟阅读
highlights:
Verda（原 DataCrunch）提供 A100、H100、H200、B200、L40S、RTX PRO 6000 等 GPU。本文解释 On-Demand、Spot、10 分钟预付结算和存储费用。

智机玄同发布于 2026年10月9日 3 分钟阅读

资料核查日期： 2026年10月9日。价格、库存和服务商规则可能变化，请以官方页面为准。

文章目录

如果你以前搜过 DataCrunch，现在看到 Verda 不要以为是另一家公司。

Verda 就是原来的 DataCrunch 品牌。

它现在已经把产品扩展成 GPU Instances、Instant Clusters、Serverless Containers 和独立存储。

## 当前 On-Demand GPU

截至 2026-10-09，Verda `/pricing` 页面公开的单 GPU On-Demand 配置包括：

- A100 SXM4 40GB：$1.37 / 小时
- A100 SXM4 80GB：$1.89 / 小时
- H100 SXM5 80GB：$3.93 / 小时
- H200 SXM5 141GB：$5.12 / 小时
- B200 SXM6 180GB：$7.42 / 小时
- L40S 48GB：$1.62 / 小时
- RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB：$2.17 / 小时

这些是 On-Demand，不是旁边更低的 Spot 价格。

## 10 分钟计费到底是什么意思

Verda 文档当前说明 PAYG 采用：

预付 10 分钟增量。

如果你在这 10 分钟结束前终止实例，未使用的部分会在下一计费周期自动退回。

所以它既不是“必须整小时”，也不是像 GPUBank 那样完全按秒实时扣。

本站因此把这一项单独标记成“预付 10 分钟”。

## A100 40GB / 80GB 都是 SXM4

这一点很重要。

Verda 官方 A100 产品页明确说明服务器使用 SXM4 模块。

所以：

- A100 SXM4 40GB
- A100 SXM4 80GB

可以和 PCIe A100 分开，不会混成一个型号。

目前 A100 SXM 80GB 已经有正式 Compare：

A100 80GB SXM 服务商价格对比

40GB SXM 暂时仍未达到 3 家门槛。

results.title: Verda explained: GPU cloud, serverless and pricing
results.author: Sequenced desk
highlights:
Verda brings several ways of running AI workloads into one GPU cloud: individual instances, multi-node clusters and serverless containers. The company previously operated as DataCrunch. Its current offer is most useful when a team needs to move between experimentation, training and deployment without pretending those workloads have identical storage, latency or billing requirements.

...

Verda’s rebrand announcement describes the transition from DataCrunch to Verda as a change of name with the same company, team and platform. The announcement set the website transition for November 2025. Older DataCrunch references therefore belong to this company history rather than a separate competing provider.

...

## 04 / Pricing The same GPU name can carry a different service price

The public pricing page separates GPU instances from serverless configurations. The entries below are USD figures consulted on 23 September 2026. CPU, memory and deployment arrangements differ between services, so the H100 rows are not interchangeable quotations for an identical bundle.

| Service | Published rate or basis | Qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100 GPU instance | $3.38 per hour | On-demand instance configuration listed on the page. |
| H100 serverless container | $3.72 per hour | Separate serverless configuration; per-replica ten-minute billing intervals. |
| Instant Clusters | On-demand per GPU-hour; reserved arrangements by quote | Confirm node topology, term and available capacity. |
| Shared filesystem | $0.20 per GiB per month shown | Confirm metered units in the quote; do not infer a converted storage total. |

Published Verda pricing and serverless billing, consulted 23 September 2026. Capacity and configuration remain subject to the current offer.

results.title: H100 GPU price per hour: 8 clouds ranked, Sep 2026
highlights:
## What is the cheapest H100 SXM or HGX price?

RunPod’s H100 SXM, at $3.49 per GPU-hour, is the cheapest SXM-class listing among the eight, checked 28 September 2026. 1 Nebius’s HGX H100 follows at $3.85, then Crusoe’s HGX H100 at $3.90 and Modal’s H100 SXM5 at $3.95. 4 5 9 The distinction matters because the top two ranked prices are both PCIe cards.

results.title: Cloud GPU Price Index: weekly median listed on-demand price of one NVIDIA H100 GPU-hour
results.author: GPU Economy
highlights: Canonical source: https://gpueconomy.com/price-index, recomputed hourly. This record is a dated snapshot (version 2026-10-02, data updated 2026-10-02T13:39:58.768836+00:00) so that a cited number keeps existing exactly as it was cited. Please cite GPU Economy and link the page. The index is the weekly median publicly listed on-demand price of one NVIDIA H100 SXM GPU-hour across the cloud GPU providers tracked by GPU Economy, in US dollars per GPU per hour, with a chain-linked base-100 companion series that moves only when a provider changes a listed price. Two files, two panels, never merged: price-index.csv is GPU Economy's own series, read hourly from each provider's price page from the week of 2026-09-07 (4 weeks in this version); price-index-history.csv is a second-hand series reconstructed from the public skypilot-org/skypilot-catalog (Apache 2.0) for the weeks before that (90 weeks, at most 7 providers). price-index.json carries the current week's constituents with the source URL behind every quote. price-index-monthly.csv holds the monthly average of the hourly index for closed months only (1 in this version), and price-index-hourly.csv the 591 hourly points those months are the mean of. Method: median, not mean, over one quote per provider and region (a provider that lists several regions enters once per region, and weighting_check in the JSON recomputes each week as a median of per-provider medians); on-demand rates only, spot and reserved excluded; node-priced offers divided by GPU count; USD-listed quotes only; marketplace floors excluded; a week is published only when at least 8 providers contributed. Full method: https://gpueconomy.com/methodology. Field definitions are in the README included with the files.
